analysis.title: The NVIDIA affair brings Trump and Xi closer
key_insights: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO on 12 November amid a US national-security probe into chip diversion to China, and was reinstated on 23 November, eleven days later. The expected destabilisation of the Trump-Xi détente did not happen.

At the APEC summit in Shenzhen the two leaders reaffirmed a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' and agreed to draft an action plan. Bessent said the H200 sales policy to China is unchanged.

Trump suggested Blackwell chips could be sold to China in two or three years, and publicly backed Huang as a 'national treasure'. NVIDIA's board cited input from 'senior levels' of the US government in reinstating him.

The affair makes the leaders co-dependent. Trump needs the relationship to deliver to defend the H200 decision before a hostile Congress, while Xi needs the back door to NVIDIA hardware until China's own AI stack can stand alone.

The détente has delivered less than hoped. NVIDIA's share of China's specialised AI hardware market fell from 95% to zero as Beijing steered firms to Huawei, allowing NVIDIA chips only for training advanced models.

Executive and legislative branches are diverging from the leaders. Commerce is tightening controls, a new rule requires a licence for any data centre worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale advanced AI compute access, and Congress is moving to codify curbs.
Democrats will control Congress from January and both parties back chip-export restrictions in the 2027 defence bill. The AI Overwatch Act would let lawmakers block sales to adversaries.

Rep. Brian Mast released records showing Commerce approved 879,868 NVIDIA H200 and equivalent AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, including firms on the Pentagon's Chinese military companies list.
NVIDIA's board set up a national security and export control committee of independent directors and is hiring a chief compliance officer. Huang is back but under watch.

Key dates are the trade truce expiry on 10 January and the G20 meeting in December. Beijing's retaliation tools are rare-earth licensing, paused but not dismantled, and a faster shift to Huawei Ascend chips.

Europe is a bystander exposed on two fronts. It depends on NVIDIA hardware, Chinese rare earths and mature chips, and the new data-centre rule could restrict its access to advanced US chips if Chinese firms trained models there.

market_movers.rationale: Huang is reinstated but under a new compliance committee, with China share at zero and tightening US export rules and legislation. A truce expiry on 10 January adds headline risk.

sector_views.rationale: China access depends on narrowing back doors, while the Trump-Xi bond supports H200 sales but Congress and Commerce are tightening controls.

risk_factors: Collapse of the Trump-Xi détente would confirm critics' claim that chips were given away for nothing.
Chinese reimposition of rare-earth export controls, paused but not dismantled.
Congress codifying chip export restrictions and removing discretion from the president.
Smuggling and remote-access routes to NVIDIA GPUs being closed by the new Commerce rule.
geopolitical: US-China détente reaffirmed at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the third Trump-Xi meeting of 2026, after Busan 2025 and Beijing in May 2026.
US-China trade truce expires on 10 January, and the two leaders meet again at the G20 in December.

New US Commerce rule effective on the summit day requires licences for data centres worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale advanced AI compute access. Beijing threatened countermeasures but did not act.
China's rare-earth export controls were lifted at Busan 2025 but could be reimposed, which would also catch the EU.
US Congress, with Democrats taking control in January, backs chip-export curbs in the 2027 defence bill and the AI Overwatch Act.

tension_points.bull_case: The leaders are co-dependent, with Trump needing the policy to deliver and Xi needing the NVIDIA back door. Both reaffirmed strategic stability at Shenzhen and Trump floated Blackwell sales in two or three years.
tension_points.bear_case: Commerce is tightening controls and Congress is moving to codify them, regardless of Trump's deals with Xi. Pressure on the back door will keep tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Expiry of the trade truce on 10 January without extension, or China reimposing rare-earth controls.

theme_stances.key_argument: The NVIDIA affair has made Trump and Xi more dependent on each other, though administrations and Congress keep tightening controls.
theme_stances.evidence: the NVIDIA affair has brought the two leaders closer, making them all the more co-dependent
